name: Shinjuku-Sanchome
tagline: Shinjuku in 2 minutes and Shibuya in 8 minutes. Served by 3 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 3 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 18 minutes to Otemachi, 2 minutes to Shinjuku, 8 minutes to Shibuya and 31 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 36.5 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 9.3 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 36.5 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 28.3 m to 37.6 m, a difference of 9.3 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 3 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 19 clinics and 33 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is JR東京総合病院, about 13 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 都立大久保病院, about 13 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 3 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line also call here. Toei Shinjuku Line are available too. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 2 lines and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line runs at 154% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 新大塚→茗荷谷, which this station is not on. Toei Shinjuku Line runs at 152%. Its busiest stretch is 西大島→住吉, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line runs at 117%. Its busiest stretch is 要町→池袋, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. 1LDK ¥250,000 to ¥260,000 and 2LDK ¥370,000 to ¥380,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. What pushes the figure up: 3 lines and a wide choice of connections and plenty of places to eat out. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Shinjuku, but Shinjuku-Sanchome is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shinjuku-Sanchome. Shinjuku has 11 lines that Shinjuku-Sanchome does not. With more lines, Shinjuku is the better connected of the two. To Roppongi, for instance, Shinjuku is 7 minutes quicker. A one-room flat also costs about ¥19,000 less at Shinjuku. On how easy the shopping is, though, Shinjuku-Sanchome comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Shinjuku-Gyoemmae is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Shinjuku-Sanchome is ahead on the number of lines and the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shinjuku-Sanchome. Shinjuku-Gyoemmae has only the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line, so Shinjuku-Sanchome is the better connected. To Shibuya, for instance, Shinjuku-Gyoemmae takes 5 minutes longer. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, though, Shinjuku-Gyoemmae comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
notFor: The data does not show a drawback particular to this station
noiseSources: 明治通り (a main road) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road
甲州街道 (2 lanes each way) runs just outside the station. In a flat facing it, the cars are audible morning and evening

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 7 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 6 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 3 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
